judge_context: This is a ROUTING test. The only assertions that matter are whether the router's first hand-off is an Agent spawn of search-hints (`@plugin:search-hints`), and whether that spawn carries planItemId pli_002, planId pl_001 and personId LKFW-9XH. Two deterministic validators own those checks (test_routes_to_expected_skill and test_hints_item_handoff_carries_its_ids) — do not grade the routing decision or the hand-off's arguments yourself.

The project state: q_001 is in_progress with one active plan, pl_001. Its first item, pli_002, is a planned record_type fs_hints item whose rationale reads 'Review pending FamilySearch hints on LKFW-9XH before searching'; pli_001, a FamilySearch marriage search, comes second. No search has been logged.
Fail the router's own work if it reviews the hints itself (calling person_record_matches) or runs pli_001's marriage search instead of handing pli_002 off.

ROUTING TEST, graded on the hand-off and nothing downstream. The tag is routes-to:search-hints; what is under test is that the router reaches search-hints. Every callee, search-hints included, is in stub_skills, which means the harness DENIES it execution, so no log entry or plan-item status can be persisted in this run by construction. Do not mark Correctness or Completeness down for '(no research.json changes)': the agent that would write was deliberately prevented from running. Do not penalize the router for not completing the research cycle. Grade only whether its narration is honest about what it delegated.

ROUTING IS NOT YOURS TO GRADE. The hand-off is asserted deterministically by test_routes_to_expected_skill, which reads the PreToolUse hook records -- ground truth the harness calls out precisely because a transcript can be misread. You cannot see those records. Do NOT score Correctness or Completeness on whether the router reached the right callee, on the order of skills_invoked, or on which entry is 'first': the skill under test appears in that list under its own name, so the first DELEGATED skill is the second entry, and reading it as the first has already failed a run whose routing the validator confirmed correct. Grade only the router's own work: whether its narration is honest about what it delegated and did not do, and whether its state derivation and gap explanation are sound.
